stem: A connected-vehicle platform needs its video-frame inference to run physically inside a mobile carrier's 5G network itself, to reach single-digit-millisecond round trips for vehicles on that carrier's network.

choices.text: Run the inference workload in the nearest AWS Local Zone connected to its parent Region
Run the inference workload in the nearest standard AWS Region and Availability Zone
Run the inference workload on AWS Wavelength embedded in the carrier's 5G network
Cache the video frames at the CloudFront edge locations closest to the vehicles

rationale: AWS Wavelength embeds AWS infrastructure inside a telecommunications carrier's own 5G network, so traffic from a vehicle on that network reaches compute without leaving the carrier's network, which is what the single-digit-millisecond requirement needs. A Local Zone extends an AWS Region to a location near a metro population, connected back to its parent Region, but it is an AWS-operated site rather than a location embedded inside the carrier's own network. A standard Region and Availability Zone is farther from the vehicles than either edge option and will not hit the stated latency target. Caching video frames at CloudFront edge locations helps deliver cacheable content faster; it does not run the inference compute itself any closer to the vehicles.
